description: Algebra is the branch of mathematics where letters (variables) are used in place of numbers. It is a highly important subject for competitive exams, involving the study of equations, polynomials, and identities.

sections.title: Basic Algebraic Identities
sections.description: These are equations that are true for all values of the variables. They are used to solve problems quickly.

sections.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
sections.description: An equation with a maximum degree of 1 is called a linear equation. Its standard form in two variables is ax + by + c = 0.

key_concepts.notation_or_symbol: x, y, z and a, b, c
key_concepts.explanation: Variables are values that can change, whereas constants are fixed numbers.

sections.title: Quadratic Equations
sections.description: An equation in which the maximum degree of the variable is 2. Its standard form is ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

sections.title: Polynomials and Remainder Theorem
sections.description: A polynomial is an algebraic expression in which the powers of variables are whole numbers.

key_concepts.explanation: If a polynomial P(x) is divided by (x - a), the remainder is P(a).
If P(a) = 0, then (x - a) is a factor of the polynomial P(x).

steps.title: Set Divisor to Zero
steps.detail: Find the value of x by equating the divisor (x - a) to 0, i.e., x = a.

steps.title: Substitute the Value
steps.detail: Substitute this value of x into the given polynomial P(x).

steps.title: Calculate
steps.detail: The resulting value P(a) is the required remainder.

sections.title: Indices and Surds
sections.description: Indices indicate how many times a number is multiplied by itself, whereas surds are irrational roots.

key_concepts.explanation: The process of removing a surd from the denominator. This is done by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate.
